chunks: The Lord of the heavens and the earth and all that lies between them, if you really do believe.

key_terms.مُوقِنِينَ: Those who are certain/believers with certainty

ai.seo_question: Who is described as the Lord of the heavens and the earth in Surah Ad-Dukhan?
ai.summary: In the context of Surah Ad-Dukhan, this verse serves as a divine challenge to the disbelievers of Mecca, linking the certainty of resurrection to the acknowledgment of Allah's sovereignty over the cosmos. Shia exegetes, such as Al-Tabarsi, highlight that 'Rabb' here implies not just creation but continuous sustenance and authority, urging believers to move from superficial certainty to deep, reflective conviction (yaqeen) in the face of divine signs.
